record.name: Barbados
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. No national AI strategy, law or regulator was found. In March 2026 the minister unveiled a digital economy plan to 2030 and spoke of the need for a secure AI framework.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

Re-ran searches in English for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified; results described the innovation ministry's 2026 budget and digital plan, the Prime Minister's reported statement that AI regulation is coming, and CARICOM's Caribbean AI Policy Roadmap. Kept low: the only government information page found refused automated access (HTTP 403), so no primary governance source is cited. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.language_note: English is an official language or an official language of national administration; it is a practical national search language for this check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The CTU table records national AI-strategy and readiness-assessment status; its country row does not substantively corroborate institute status or establish independence from national reporting. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.

record.notes: Thin evidence. Barbados Today (11 Mar 2026) reports a $188m digital economy plan to 2030 in which the minister described a robust digital ID system or a secure AI framework as 21st-century infrastructure; no framework text was found. The Central Bank of Barbados published a summary of a public lecture on AI policy (Dec 2024), which is not a policy. The CTU report (July 2026) lists 'None reported' for a national AI strategy.

next_check.reason: Look for the secure AI framework or a national AI policy.
